cards.back: A complete loop that electricity can flow around, with a source such as a cell.
cards.say: electric circuit. A complete loop that electricity can flow around, with a source such as a cell.

cards.back: A source of electrical energy that pushes current around a circuit.
cards.say: cell. A source of electrical energy that pushes current around a circuit.

cards.back: Two or more cells joined together.
cards.say: battery. Two or more cells joined together.

cards.front: How do you draw a cell in a circuit diagram?
cards.back: As two parallel lines, one long and one short. The long line is the positive end.
cards.say: How do you draw a cell in a circuit diagram? As two parallel lines, one long and one short. The long line is the positive end.

cards.back: A component that gives out light when current flows through it.
cards.say: bulb. A component that gives out light when current flows through it.

cards.back: A component that opens or closes a circuit to turn it off or on.
cards.say: switch. A component that opens or closes a circuit to turn it off or on.

cards.back: When there is a gap, so no current flows and the bulb is off.
cards.say: When is a switch open? When there is a gap, so no current flows and the bulb is off.

cards.back: When it joins the circuit, so current flows and the bulb comes on.
cards.say: When is a switch closed? When it joins the circuit, so current flows and the bulb comes on.

cards.front: What is needed for a bulb to light?
cards.back: A complete circuit with no gaps, and a cell or battery.
cards.say: What is needed for a bulb to light? A complete circuit with no gaps, and a cell or battery.

cards.back: A component that makes a sound when current flows through it.
cards.say: buzzer. A component that makes a sound when current flows through it.

cards.back: A component that spins when current flows through it.
cards.say: motor. A component that spins when current flows through it.

cards.back: The flow of electric charge around a circuit. It is measured in amps.
cards.say: current. The flow of electric charge around a circuit. It is measured in amps.

cards.back: How strongly a cell pushes the current. It is measured in volts.
cards.say: voltage. How strongly a cell pushes the current. It is measured in volts.

cards.front: Why do circuit diagrams use symbols?
cards.back: They are quick to draw and everyone can read them.
cards.say: Why do circuit diagrams use symbols? They are quick to draw and everyone can read them.

cards.front: Why do we draw circuit wires with straight lines and corners?
cards.back: It keeps the diagram clear and easy to read.
cards.say: Why do we draw circuit wires with straight lines and corners? It keeps the diagram clear and easy to read.

cards.front: What happens to the brightness of a bulb if you add another cell in series?
cards.back: The bulb gets brighter, because more current flows.
cards.say: What happens to the brightness of a bulb if you add another cell in series? The bulb gets brighter, because more current flows.

cards.front: What happens to the brightness of bulbs if you add more bulbs in series?
cards.back: They get dimmer, because the current is shared.
cards.say: What happens to the brightness of bulbs if you add more bulbs in series? They get dimmer, because the current is shared.

cards.back: A circuit with only one path for the current. All components are in one loop.
cards.say: series circuit. A circuit with only one path for the current. All components are in one loop.

cards.back: A circuit with more than one path for the current.
cards.say: parallel circuit. A circuit with more than one path for the current.

cards.front: In a series circuit, what happens if one bulb blows?
cards.back: All the bulbs go out, because the circuit is broken.
cards.say: In a series circuit, what happens if one bulb blows? All the bulbs go out, because the circuit is broken.

cards.front: In a parallel circuit, what happens if one bulb blows?
cards.back: The other bulbs stay on, because they have their own paths.
cards.say: In a parallel circuit, what happens if one bulb blows? The other bulbs stay on, because they have their own paths.

cards.front: Which is brighter: two bulbs in series or two bulbs in parallel with the same battery?
cards.back: Parallel. Each bulb gets the full push of the battery.
cards.say: Which is brighter: two bulbs in series or two bulbs in parallel with the same battery? Parallel. Each bulb gets the full push of the battery.

cards.front: What do we call a material that lets current flow?
cards.back: A conductor. Metals are conductors.
cards.say: What do we call a material that lets current flow? A conductor. Metals are conductors.

cards.front: What happens to a motor if you add more cells?
cards.back: It spins faster.
cards.say: What happens to a motor if you add more cells? It spins faster.
